references.text: The context that establishes Israel's role as God's treasured people, which forms the basis for describing them as a kingdom of priests.
Israel is described as a holy nation (גוי קדוש) to the Lord, chosen from among all peoples on earth.
Israel is called a holy nation to the Lord, chosen to be His treasured people.
The Lord confirms that Israel shall be His treasured people and a holy nation, exalted above all nations.
The prophecy that Israel will be called the Lord's priests and God's servants, fulfilling the promise of a royal priesthood.
Believers are described as living stones being built up into a holy priesthood to offer spiritual sacrifices.
Direct quotation and application of Exodus 19:6 to the Christian church: a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation.
Christ has made believers a kingdom and priests to God, fulfilling the promise in Exodus 19:6.
The saved are made a kingdom and priests to God, who will reign on earth.
Those who share in the first resurrection will be priests of God and of Christ and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
The Sabbath in 31:13 serves as the practical sign of the identity established as 'a royal priesthood and holy nation' in 19:6.
The deliverance in 6:6 is the necessary prerequisite for the people to become a royal priesthood in 19:6.
Hebrews 8:10 shows the inner transformation that makes it possible to fully live out the identity of 'God's people' from Exodus 19:6.
The contrast between the calling of the entire nation as a royal priesthood (19:6) and the prophet's role as a watchman (3:17) when the people fail in this calling.
